author: claude
desc: Separate the two things ticket 221 conflated. Round 11 concluded the gP13/gP19 SMC key writes break 14-core boot because removing pwren-gpios fixed it -- but pwren-gpios ALSO powers the PCIe endpoints, so removing it stops brcmfmac, hci_bcm4377 and sdhci-pci probing and removes all their DMA. Verified: every DTB that boots 14 cores has pwren-gpios count 0; the only one that hangs has 2. So the sound statement is only that something in the chain SMC-key-write -> endpoint-power -> driver-probe -> endpoint-DMA breaks the boot. TEST: keep pwren-gpios (SMC write happens, endpoints power up) but build WITHOUT the endpoint drivers -- disable BRCMFMAC, BT_HCIBCM4377, MMC_SDHCI_PCI. 14 cores boot => SMC write and power-up innocent, an endpoint driver's DMA is the culprit; bisect one at a time, brcmfmac first (large firmware DMA through the DART). Still hangs => drivers innocent and round 11's SMC-write conclusion is restored on sound evidence. ALSO: the macOS GPIO value 0x00800001 (vs CMD_OUTPUT|1) was tested at 14 cores and does NOT fix the hang -- refuted, experiment reverted. AND get DOCKCHANNEL_EARLYCON output: the 14-core hang is still pass/fail with zero diagnosis, which is the main thing slowing this down. RESULT 2026-08-03 (valid re-run): lease live, maxcpus=14 asserted from dcuart-boot.log, logs deleted before each boot. CONTROL endpoint drivers ON = hang (20 lines). EXPERIMENT endpoint drivers OFF (BRCMFMAC/BT_HCIBCM4377/MMC_SDHCI_PCI disabled, kbuild-asserted) with pwren-gpios still present = ALSO hang (20 lines). So ENDPOINT DRIVERS ARE EXONERATED -- their DMA is not the cause, and round 11s conclusion is restored: the trigger is the gP13/gP19 SMC key write and the port power-up it performs. CRITICAL PROCESS NOTE: the rig lease (1 h) expired during round 12 and rig-guard refused every boot; because the boot script was invoked with >/dev/null the refusal was invisible and STALE logs were read as results (identical 535-line counts, maxcpus=1 regardless of what was passed). INVALIDATED and needing re-run: the macOS GPIO value test at 14 cores, the first 223 run, and BOTH earlycon attempts -- the claim "the kernel dies before earlycon initialises" is WITHDRAWN. New standing rules: never suppress rig-script output; delete the log before each boot and treat a short log as "boot did not happen"; assert the cmdline from dcuart-boot.log every run; renew the lease per batch. ROUND 14 2026-08-03: macOS GPIO value re-tested under VALID methodology (lease renewed, logs deleted per boot, maxcpus=14 asserted from dcuart-boot.log, output not suppressed, endpoint drivers enabled, TWO runs): both HANG. So writing macOS 0x00800001 instead of CMD_OUTPUT|1 does NOT fix the 14-core hang -- the refutation now stands on real evidence, and gpio-macsmc should NOT be changed on the strength of sol decode (which is itself correct; the values do differ, it is just not the cause). Experiment reverted, known-good kernel rebuilt, 1-core SD-root desktop verified back up. NEXT HIGHEST VALUE: real diagnostics for the 14-core hang -- it is still pass/fail with zero visibility. Options: earlycon=dockchannel with the CORRECT data-window address taken from the DT (not a guess); m1n1-side tracing of the SMC key write; or bisect WHICH key (gP13 WiFi vs gP19 SD) triggers it, which is cheap and might permit WiFi at full core count before the mechanism is understood. ROUND 15 KEY BISECT 2026-08-03 (full methodology: lease live, logs deleted per boot, maxcpus=14 asserted, REFUSE count 0): pwren-wifi-only (gP13 = BCM4388 WL_REG_ON) = HANG (20 lines); pwren-sd-only (gP19 = SD power) = 14 CPUs BOOT (530 lines). So gP13 ALONE causes the pre-console hang and gP19 is harmless -- the trigger is specifically POWERING THE BCM4388 WiFi/BT MODULE, and since brcmfmac is exonerated it is the chip coming up, not a driver. DECISIVE EVIDENCE FOR TWO SEPARATE BUGS: (A) the gP13 pre-console hang, deterministic, avoidable; (B) bulk-store corruption into freshly allocated pages, intermittent, present from 2 cores up. Booting pwren-sd-only at 14 cores avoids A and EXPOSES B: 14 CPUs up, SD mounted, switch_root, OpenRC starts (532 lines) then USERSPACE DIES (ttydc0 shell never answers). So avoiding gP13 buys a 14-CPU KERNEL, not a 14-core daily driver -- nothing shippable, maxcpus=1 remains the only working userspace. VALUE: bug A is bounded to one key write powering one chip; and pwren-sd-only at 14 cores is now the best available HARNESS for studying bug B without A masking it. NEXT: (1) bug A -- try the ADT function-pcie_port_control PrtC(0x57) step and the 100 ms wlan_reg_on_on_delay we never implemented (two-line change); (2) bug B -- run scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh on the pwren-sd-only 14-core harness with per-step /dev/kmsg output; (3) both still need earlycon working for pre-console diagnosis. ROUND 16 2026-08-03: went to implement the "ADT delay + PrtC" next step and found it rested on TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS. (1) There is NO wlan_reg_on_on_delay property anywhere in either ADT capture -- WITHDRAWN. (2) pcie-apple ALREADY does msleep(100) Tpvperl right after gpiod_set_value(pwren,1), so "add the missing delay" was never an available change. (3) PrtC(0x57) is NOT a two-line change: its provider is phandle 86 = /arm-io/apcie0 (apcie,t6040), i.e. a PCIe-CONTROLLER platform function, so it needs kernelcache RE -- handed to sol as ticket 225. Also confirmed function-reg_on = pKW4(gP13, 0x800000), which with the on-bit is 0x800001 and matches sols decode exactly, so the ADT holds no unused information about the write. Bug A is therefore bounded but unexplained, with every cheap avenue closed; my productive direction is bug B on the pwren-sd-only 14-core harness plus getting earlycon working.
